body.intent: Build a full in-editor development chat interface for the insrc VS Code extension, backed by the user's existing Claude/Codex CLI subscriptions (via the daemon's CliProvider concept), NOT Copilot's paid token allowance. The extension itself spawns and streams the claude/codex CLI subprocess directly for chat turns (using each CLI's structured JSON stream mode, e.g. claude --output-format stream-json), bypassing the daemon for execution, while grounding stays via the same daemon protocol delivered by the CLI's own insrc MCP tool calls (the Claude-Code model). It is a general-purpose passthrough chat (free-form asks/coding) presented as a custom Webview panel whose CORE CHAT PANEL has a TERMINAL look & feel — monospace type, box-drawing chrome, phosphor accents matching the insrc docs-site TUI aesthetic (site/css/tui.css) — explicitly NOT a chat-bubble/message-box experience; streaming reads like terminal output and lifecycle markers render as terminal-style status lines. Scope: persistent extension-local chat history + a history dropdown; a per-chat provider selector across the agentic coding CLIs (claude/codex); native per-CLI session-resume continuity; real-time streaming with per-turn lifecycle markers (thinking/tool-call/streaming/done, enriched by observing the CLI's insrc MCP calls); a per-session auto (visualize-only) vs review (extension-gated accept/reject) inline-diff view for code edits; and a VS Code docs-review pane (built in this epic, mirroring the JetBrains panel) that lists daemon pendingApproval workflow artifacts and acts on them via insrc_workflow_approve. UX mocks (terminal-styled) of the chat panel, dropdowns, inline-diff view and docs-review pane are an explicit deliverable, produced at the design stage.
body.scopeBoundary: VS Code ships first; JetBrains parity is a later phase and out of scope for this spec. The chat is a passthrough dev-chat surface, NOT the UI that orchestrates the tracked insrc workflow (the CLI drives that itself via its MCP + steering). Execution of the chat CLI is extension-managed and deliberately bypasses the daemon; chat history is extension-local and NOT stored in the daemon; session continuity uses native CLI resume/session-id, not extension-replayed history; providers cannot be switched mid-chat (switching starts a new chat); the provider set is the agentic coding CLIs (claude/codex) only — Ollama is deliberately excluded (it is a plain-completion model, not an agentic coding CLI); and the docs-review pane acts only on daemon-tracked workflow artifacts, not ad-hoc chat-generated docs. Webview-panel multiplicity (single active panel vs concurrent panels) is deferred to the design stage with a single-active-panel default.

decisions.chosen: Extension-managed: the VS Code extension itself spawns and streams the claude/codex CLI subprocess directly, bypassing the daemon
ruledOut: Daemon-managed: the daemon owns a CliProvider subprocess per chat session and streams tokens back to the extension over the existing Unix-socket IPC (new streaming IPC method)
Hybrid: daemon owns the session record and persisted history, but the extension spawns/streams the CLI process itself and reports the transcript back to the daemon asynchronously
decisions.reason: This is foundational: it determines how streaming, session/history persistence, and future JetBrains parity are built, and it interacts directly with the repo's 'Daemon owns all DB access / IPC-only' and 'Cloud LLM access goes through CliProvider' architectural rules.

decisions.chosen: Daemon-sourced: extension calls daemon IPC (e.g. analyze) to fetch a graph-grounded context bundle before each turn, then feeds it into the CLI prompt
ruledOut: Extension-local: extension gathers context itself (open editor files, selections, cursor position, workspace text search) with no daemon call

Hybrid: extension always attaches local editor context (open files/selection) and additionally calls daemon analyze on-demand for deeper graph-grounded context when the user's ask needs it (e.g. 'who calls this', cross-file reasoning)
User-toggle: a per-chat setting lets the user pick 'local only' vs 'daemon-grounded' context mode explicitly
decisions.reason: Now that the extension itself spawns the CLI, where does the chat's codebase CONTEXT come from — does it still go through the daemon's graph, or does the extension assemble it locally?

decisions.chosen: Extension-local: history stored purely in VS Code (workspaceState/globalState or local JSON files), independent of the daemon
ruledOut: Daemon-persisted: extension writes each turn to the daemon over IPC into the existing session-vec/turn-vec Lance tables; history is fetched the same way for the dropdown
Hybrid: extension keeps a fast local cache for the history dropdown, and asynchronously mirrors turns into the daemon's session-vec/turn-vec for durability + future search
decisions.reason: insrc's storage layer already ships session-vec / turn-vec Lance tables (per db/lance/ in the project structure) and the project's key architectural rule is 'daemon owns all DB access — CLI, MCP, and the IDE workbench communicate via IPC only.' Execution itself was just decided to bypass the daemon, but that rule governs persistence, not CLI spawning.

decisions.chosen: General-purpose passthrough chat: free-form asks/coding; markers show per-turn CLI status (thinking/tool-call/streaming/done); the tracked insrc workflow stays a separate surface the user invokes deliberately, not auto-driven by this chat
ruledOut: Workflow-driving chat: feature-shaped turns are auto-routed through triage→the routed workflow, and lifecycle markers ARE the workflow stages (brainstorm/define/design/build/review); the chat becomes the primary UI for the tracked pipeline
Split: free-form chat by default, with a visible mode toggle/slash-command that opts a given conversation into the tracked-workflow path; lifecycle markers only appear in that mode
decisions.reason: Is this a general-purpose free-form CLI chat (like an in-editor dev session, any ask/any coding task) whose 'stage markers' are just per-turn CLI activity status — or is it purpose-built as the UI that drives insrc's tracked feature workflow (brainstorm→triage→define→design→build→review), with lifecycle markers reflecting those workflow phases?

decisions.chosen: Dual/configurable: a per-session toggle between auto (visualize-only) and review (extension-gated)
ruledOut: Visualize-only: let the CLI's own permission/approval mode (interactive prompt, auto-accept, plan mode, etc.) decide whether an edit lands; the extension just renders whatever change appears on disk as an inline diff, in every mode
Extension-gated: intercept the CLI's edit/write tool calls itself and always show an inline diff with accept/reject before the write reaches disk, overriding the CLI's own auto-accept behavior
decisions.reason: For code edits the CLI subprocess makes, does the extension only VISUALIZE edits after the CLI's own permission mode has already applied them, or does it GATE every edit itself with an accept/reject inline diff before the write reaches disk?

decisions.chosen: Providers are the agentic coding CLIs only (claude/codex); Ollama is excluded from scope
ruledOut: Include Ollama as a chat provider via its local HTTP API (localhost:11434)
Include Ollama by spawning `ollama run <model>` as a CLI subprocess
Route Ollama turns through daemon IPC, reusing the existing OllamaProvider
decisions.reason: Ollama is a plain-completion model, not an agentic coding CLI (no native tool-use, file edits, or insrc MCP grounding), so it does not fit a coding-chat surface whose value is agentic edits + grounded tool calls. The provider set is limited to the agentic coding CLIs; future integration with other agentic coding CLIs (e.g. OpenCode) is deferred to a later phase.

decisions.chosen: Native session resume: use each provider CLI's own resume/session flag (e.g. claude --resume, a codex session id) so the CLI itself keeps conversation state between turns
ruledOut: Full-history replay: spawn a fresh CLI process every turn and re-supply the full prior conversation plus a fresh context bundle as part of the prompt
Long-lived interactive subprocess: keep one CLI process alive per open chat tab, streaming turns over its stdin/stdout for the life of the session
decisions.reason: Follows directly from decision 1 (chat-execution-ownership: extension spawns/streams the CLI itself) and interacts with decision 2 (context-sourcing: a fresh context bundle is fetched per turn regardless of which continuity model is chosen).

decisions.chosen: Custom Webview panel — our own React/HTML chat surface with full control over message list, dropdowns, and embedded diff/docs-review widgets
ruledOut: Native Chat Participant API — register into VS Code's built-in Chat sidebar (@mentions, familiar chat UX, streaming/markdown rendering for free)
Hybrid — a thin native Chat Participant as a discoverable entry point that deep-links into the real custom Webview panel
decisions.reason: This gates every remaining UI decision (diff rendering, dropdown placement, docs-review integration) and interacts with the 'not Copilot's tokens' goal, since VS Code's native Chat view has historically been surfaced by the Copilot Chat extension shell even when the model/provider behind a participant is not Copilot's.

decisions.chosen: Structured JSON stream mode: invoke each CLI with its machine-readable streaming flag (e.g. claude --output-format stream-json; codex's equivalent event-stream mode) and parse discrete JSON event objects per turn
ruledOut: Plain-text heuristics: run the CLI in its normal interactive/plain-text mode and infer lifecycle state by pattern-matching stdout (e.g. lines starting with 'Reading', diff-looking hunks, a trailing prompt)
Hybrid: use structured JSON stream mode wherever the CLI supports it (claude, and codex if available), fall back to plain-text heuristics only for providers without one
decisions.reason: The extension needs discrete events (thinking / tool-call / file-edit / done) out of the claude/codex CLI subprocess to drive lifecycle markers and to detect edits for the inline diff view. How should it get those events out of the running subprocess?

decisions.chosen: In scope: build a VS Code docs-review webview view (mirroring the JetBrains review/comment/accept/reject panel) as part of this epic, embedded alongside the chat panel
ruledOut: Out of scope: leave generated-docs review unimplemented for VS Code in this spec; file it as a separate follow-up epic
Minimal seam only: the webview renders docs read-only and links out to the existing approval flow (insrc_workflow_approve / TUI) for actual accept/reject, deferring a full custom review UI
decisions.reason: You described the generated-docs review surface (review/comment/accept/reject) as 'already built' — but that panel exists only on the JetBrains side (the IDE artifact-review panel epic was JetBrains-only, never shipped to VS Code). VS Code currently has no equivalent widget. Given that, should building a VS Code docs-review UI be part of THIS chat-interface spec, or handled separately?

decisions.chosen: Fixed per chat: provider is chosen when a chat is created; trying a different provider always means starting a NEW chat with its own native session.
ruledOut: Switchable mid-chat with context replay: changing the dropdown starts a fresh native session under the new provider and the extension re-primes it with prior turns as context.
Switchable mid-chat via auto-fork: changing the dropdown splits off a new, linked chat-history entry under the new provider with no context replay — the new provider starts cold.
decisions.reason: The provider/CLI selector dropdown (decision 8's chat UI) sits alongside native per-provider session resume (decision 7). Can a user switch the provider mid-conversation within one chat, or is the provider fixed for that chat's lifetime?

decisions.chosen: Daemon-tracked workflow artifacts only: pane lists pendingApproval artifacts (Epic/HLD/LLD/DEF/Story) via daemon IPC, and accept/reject calls insrc_workflow_approve / the review flow — a direct port of the JetBrains panel's data model, independent of this chat's own turns
ruledOut: Ad-hoc chat-generated docs only: pane reviews markdown/docs the CLI produces during a free-form turn (e.g. "write API docs for this"); accept writes the file to disk, reject discards — purely local, no daemon IPC
Unified: the same pane renders both daemon workflow artifacts and local ad-hoc chat-generated docs, tagged by origin, with accept behaving differently per origin (IPC approve vs write-to-disk)
decisions.reason: The docs-review pane mirrors the JetBrains review/comment/accept/reject panel, which operates on daemon-tracked workflow artifacts (Epic/HLD/LLD/DEF pending approval). But this chat is a general-purpose passthrough, separate from the tracked workflow (decision 4). What should the VS Code docs-review pane actually list and act on?
